Title: The tick: two compositions of one city step
Approach: Sim.gd._process calls RoseSim.step 2 times a second (8 at most a frame); RoseSim.step re-composes game::handoff, nerve, cargo, trade, ivan, pressure, shift::work_cycle and campaign::onboard itself. The proofs call World::tick, which composes the same functions in its own order. Both copies are edited by hand on every feature (PAC-083 wired the work clock twice).
Exports: the drift list (OVR-006); the one tick (OVR-011, OVR-013)
Check: read of both functions side by side

Title: The shift's end and start
Approach: Sim.gd.end_shift calls RoseSim.colony_end_shift(people, stash, day) then refresh_movers(people, day + 1); the bridge re-composes loops::play, end_shift, breach::shift_end, pressure::end, trade::end_shift, campaign::shift_end, threats.start_shift and ivan::shift_end. World::end_shift composes the same, then movers() and trade_start().
Check: read of both paths side by side

Title: The founding
Approach: Sim.gd.ensure calls configure_run, start_city, set_strata_open, found_city, bind_stash and refresh_movers on four objects (RoseSim, RoseStash, RosePeople, RoseProfile). World::found_with founds the same city in one call. The game founds the Stash in RoseStash.found and the roster in RosePeople.found, outside the sim.
Check: read of both paths

Title: Campaign state held outside Rust
Approach: Sim.gd holds day, corpses, route_runs, route_memory, stranded, last_outcome and launch as GDScript dictionaries; RoseStash holds the Stash, ledger, bench, item table and recipes; RosePeople the roster, traits, names and the shift's dead. The save crate already has fields for corpses and route memory (SaveFile.corpses, .route_memory) that nothing fills. A save of RoseSim alone would lose the corpses on the routes and the route memory.
Check: read of Sim.gd and the save crate

Title: Data loading: the game reads disk, the proofs read the binary
Approach: The bridge's data_text reads res://../data/<file> and, when the file is missing or fails to parse, silently uses the copy compiled in. World uses the compiled ::shipped() files. So an edit to data/*.toml changes the live game (debug) and leaves every proof unchanged until cargo build, and a malformed edit falls back without a word. The README's 'balancing never recompiles' holds for the game only.
Check: read of every data_text and shipped() call

Approach: Six differences where CURRENT-STATE names one: (1) guard posts follow every work cycle in the bridge, only the shift's start in World; (2) campaign::onboard also runs at the shift's start in the bridge; (3) the breach re-opens the Board's strata and the raider roll in the bridge, while World keeps S1's raiders for good; (4) the bridge lays recover bodies (trade::end_shift with a Board), World passes None; (5) the handoff's Strainbook card is dated colony.shift in the bridge, one behind the day from the second shift, and the day in World; (6) data from disk against compiled data (OVR-005). Items 3 and 4 mean the proofs never meet escalating raiders or recover contracts' bodies.
